senses.gloss:
Sañjaya
------------------------------------------
Son of Govalgaṇa—who was a minister of the blind king धृतराष्ट्र, as also his charioteer—Sañjaya is a well-known character in the great epic, the Mahābhārata.
He used to stay most of the time with Dhṛtarāṣṭa. He had advised the blind king several times not to ill-treat or alienate the Pāṇḍavas but to no avail.
Before the कुरुक्षेत्र war, he had been sent to the Pāṇḍavas as a messenger of peace, which was an entirely one-sided affair! Naturally, the Pāṇḍavas as per कृष्ण’s advice, rejected it.
During the war he used to describe it to the blind king with a running commentary since he had been specially endowed with a divine sight by the great sage व्यास. He lost it after the war was over.
Though he too fought in the war on the side of the Kauravas, he did not die since his life was saved by the sage.
After धृतराष्ट्र and गान्धारी perished in the forest fire he retired to the Himalayas.
